correctness.rationale: For each squarefree n, sigma_-3(n) is exactly the product of local factors 1+p^-3. The prime tail beyond seven satisfies the complete-subsums condition: for p=11,13,17,19,23 the next-five-prime products are strictly larger by verified exact rational comparisons; for all p>=29, Nagura 1952 yields q_j<(6/5)^j p, and logarithmic lower bounds give a coefficient 2079146625/1513630118>1. The elementary greedy subsum lemma then proves the tail closure is [1,U]. All sixteen head coefficients over 2,3,5,7 are distinct; their exact minimum consecutive ratio is 344/343. The elementary odd-reciprocal bound gives log U<1/500 and hence U<500/499<344/343. Thus all fifteen gaps are strict, without assuming the finite enumeration proves an infinite statement. The published prime-interval theorem is an explicit external premise, and the exact-rational verifier replayed successfully.

value.rationale: Defant explicitly asks to determine the number of connected components for fixed restricted-domain parameters k and r. The natural k=1 (squarefree), r=3 case is answered exactly with sixteen closed intervals and all endpoints in finite-prime/Euler-product form; a structural prime-tail lemma and a sharp four-prime separation certificate explain the result. This is an infinite range-closure classification, not arbitrary finite tabulation, while the full parameter-dependent problem remains unresolved.
